paragraphs.text: Learner drivers who take lessons once a week usually need about 45 hours of lessons before passing. Those who take two lessons a week often need fewer hours in total, because they forget less between lessons.
Practising with a family member between lessons can help, but instructors warn that parents may pass on bad habits, such as holding the steering wheel with one hand.
The theory test includes a section on recognising hazards, which is shown as video clips. Many learners fail this part because they react too late or click too often.
On the day of the practical test, candidates are allowed to take their instructor with them in the car. This can calm nerves, although the instructor may not speak during the test.
Nearly half of all candidates fail their first practical test, although many pass at the second attempt. The most common reasons are not checking mirrors and not looking carefully at junctions.

Shared offices, where freelancers and small companies rent desks by the day or month, have become popular in many cities. The cheapest option is usually a hot desk, which means users sit wherever there is a free space.
Members who pay more can have a fixed desk, where they can leave their computer and papers overnight. Private rooms for teams are also available but cost several times more.
Most shared offices include internet, printing and coffee in the price. Meeting rooms can usually be booked free of charge for a limited number of hours each month.
Many members say the main benefit is not the desk but the people. Regular social events help freelancers meet potential clients and avoid feeling isolated.
However, open shared spaces can be noisy, and some members find it hard to concentrate. Most offices provide phone booths for private calls. Some also have a separate quiet room.
